topic: Multi-instance and RobloxPlayerBeta.exe process behaviour on Windows (client 0.730-0.744, Jul-Oct 2026)

findings.claim: The current client binary contains both singleton names, ROBLOX_singletonEvent and ROBLOX_singletonMutex, as plain ASCII with no Local\ or Global\ prefix. They sit only in RobloxPlayerBeta.exe, not in the DLL, installer or crash handler.
findings.detail: Static check, nothing executed. Each name appears once as ASCII and never as UTF-16LE in RobloxPlayerBeta.exe from version-02c37bc51a384b8f (Oct 5), version-11f155f3450f4c8e (Oct 19) and version-9ac8595712b447a7 (0.744.0.7441080, Oct 24, 145,404,368 bytes). In the current exe, "ROBLOX_singletonEvent" is at file offset 0x714eb10 and "ROBLOX_singletonMutex" at 0x714eb28. Neither name appears in RobloxPlayerBeta.dll (18 MB, new exe+dll split), RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe or RobloxCrashHandler.exe. The Hyperion packing does not hide these .rdata strings. Strings next to them: "[FLog::WndProcessCheck] Cannot create event to secure single process: {}", "Failure creating named (preventing multiple simultaneous processes): {}", "waitForNewPlayerProcess new waiting for mutex result is {:#08X}, ERROR {}", "WindowsAppReloadTelemetry CreateEventFailure / CreateMutexFailure / MutexWaitResultLoopUpdate / EventWaitResultUpdate", "Failure waiting on named event (preventing multiple simultaneous processes): {}" and "Waiting for event before showing window: {}". There is also a separate new guard: "B:\Client\WindowsClient\SingleInstanceGuard.cpp", with the settings SingleInstanceGuardTimeoutMilliSec and SingleInstanceGuardReadHwndRetries. It names objects with the UTF-16 formats "{}.mtx" and "{}.shm" (a mutex plus shared memory holding the active client HWND), with messages "NO active client window, cannot send deep links" and "Failed to send deeplink, result: %lld, error: %u". Its base name could not be recovered statically. Because the names have no prefix, a normal user process creates them in \Sessions\<n>\BaseNamedObjects, the same directory as Local\. MultiAlt's code comment reports the live object as \Sessions\<n>\BaseNamedObjects\ROBLOX_singletonEvent.
sources: local static scan: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\Versions\version-9ac8595712b447a7\RobloxPlayerBeta.exe (grep -a + python -I UTF-16LE scan)

findings.claim: By default the client allows only one instance by replacing the old one: starting a second RobloxPlayerBeta.exe signals ROBLOX_singletonEvent, and the running client then shuts itself down cleanly.
findings.detail: Local logs show this happening. In 0.743.0.7431129_20261015T175303Z_Player_10630_last.log (the old client), at 18:47:36.688 the lines are "[FLog::WndProcessCheck] WindowsAppReloadTelemetry EventWaitResultUpdate", then "[FLog::Systray] Main thread: Received close main window request", "[FLog::SingleSurfaceApp] shutDown: (stage:UGCGame).", "leaveUGCGameInternal", "Disconnected from server for reason: Player: 285 (DisconnectClientInitiated)", and then the process exits. The new client, 20261015T184736Z_Player_DDC69, logged "waitForNewPlayerProcess new waiting for mutex result is 0X000080" (WAIT_ABANDONED) and then "0X000000" (WAIT_OBJECT_0). Every normal start logs "waitForNewPlayerProcess ... result is 0X000000, ERROR The operation completed successfully." followed by "MutexWaitResultLoopUpdate" (61 of 61 recent logs). So the event triggers the replacement and the mutex is waited on during the handover. The exact order of calls and the timeouts are inferred, not disassembled.

findings.claim: The event name dates to 2023. Holding only ROBLOX_singletonMutex (the old Roblox Account Manager and Bloxstrap method) stopped preventing the replacement around July-August 2025. Pre-creating a MUTEX named ROBLOX_singletonEvent works today.
findings.detail:
Timeline:
(a) Dashbloxx/MultiRoblox commit 95d6020c on 2023-06-12 changed CreateMutex(0,1,L"ROBLOX_singletonMutex") to L"ROBLOX_singletonEvent", so the event existed by June 2023.
(b) ic3w0lf22 Roblox Account Manager (archived, last push 2024-10-01) uses new Mutex(true, "ROBLOX_singletonMutex").
(c) Bloxstrap MultiInstanceWatcher (commit d244f42b, 2025-03-15) used new Mutex(false, "ROBLOX_singletonMutex") + WaitOne(0) before launching Roblox.
(d) Issues from July-August 2025 report that the new instance overwrites the first: Bloxstrap #5635 (2025-08-05) and #5579 (2025-07-28).
(e) Bloxstrap removed the feature in v2.10.0 (commit 1a63b597, 2025-09-30; release 2025-10-01: "Multi-instance launching (roblox broke it)").
(f) Bloxstrap #6054 (2025-11-20, tested by contributor RealMeddsam) reports that creating a mutex called ROBLOX_singletonEvent before launch works.
(g) MultiBloxy (code last changed 2024-11-23) does new Mutex(false, "ROBLOX_singletonEvent").
(h) evanovar/RobloxAccountManager (the most active, Oct 2026) calls CreateMutexW(NULL, TRUE, name) for "ROBLOX_SingletonEvent", "ROBLOX_singletonEvent" and "ROBLOX_singletonMutex", with no namespace prefix. Only the exact-case "ROBLOX_singletonEvent" exists in the binary, so the capitalised variant is redundant.
(i) MultiAlt tests a_reserved_name_cannot_be_created_as_an_event, which shows that once a mutex holds the name, CreateEventW of the same name fails (type mismatch, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE). The client then logs "Cannot create event to secure single process" and continues. That last step is inferred from the tools working, not observed in a local log.

findings.claim: How maintained tools do multi-instance today: (1) create and hold named objects before any client starts (evanovar default mode, MultiBloxy, MultiAlt mutex), or (2) close the ROBLOX_singletonEvent handle inside running clients (MultiBloxy HandleCloser fallback, evanovar Handle64 mode, MultiAlt singleton.rs). Bloxstrap no longer offers multi-instance, and Fishstrap's current source has no singleton code.
findings.detail: Option (1) only works if no RobloxPlayerBeta.exe is running yet: evanovar refuses with ROBLOX_RUNNING, and MultiAlt notes the mutex 'only works preventively'. Option (2) uses NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemExtendedHandleInformation 0x40), NtQueryObject(ObjectNameInformation) and DuplicateHandle(..., DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE) after OpenProcess(PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE), and works without elevation according to MultiAlt. RoALT has ruled this option out. MultiAlt's experimental 'ReserveSingletonEvent' re-creates a Mutex named ROBLOX_singletonEvent right after closing handles, because a client that teleports between places re-runs the single-instance check and may close a sibling. That teleport claim comes from MultiAlt's docs and is unverified. Fishstrap's current main branch (Bootstrapper.cs, LaunchHandler.cs) has no ROBLOX_singleton references, only its own '<ProjectName>-Bootstrapper' mutex and a ConfirmLaunches check via Mutex.TryOpenExisting("ROBLOX_singletonMutex"). Bloxstrap's LaunchHandler.cs still has that same TryOpenExisting check (ConfirmLaunches only).

findings.claim: In Roblox's own 'tray' A/B treatment, closing the window spawns a NEW RobloxPlayerBeta.exe in tray mode, which takes over the singleton and keeps running in the background. A process ending is therefore not the only signal that a game window closed, and a Roblox process may already exist before RoALT starts.
findings.detail:
Binary strings: "--launch-to-tray", "[FLog::Systray] Successfully launched new process in systray mode", "User exit app and stay in tray mode for {} seconds", "Systray menu item Exit is clicked", "Auto startup is enabled", "set auto start registry failed: {}", "Starting background update timers", "SetPriorityClass(IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS)".
Every 0.743 log (Oct 2026) has "[FLog::Systray] Tray treatment is ON)" and "In Tray ELT Treatment group". In 0.730.23.7300792_20260720T162120Z_Player_149CD_last.log at 16:26:34 the order is: "Successfully launched new process in systray mode", then "EventWaitResultUpdate", then "shutDown: (stage:UGCGame)." The new process's log, 20260720T162636Z_Player_8A4E8, shows "Systray initialized in sync mode", takes the mutex (0X000000), runs update timers, and stays until the user clicks "Exit" in the tray. The same pattern appears in Sept 2026 logs.
If a tray process is alive, it holds ROBLOX_singletonEvent. Then RoALT cannot create its mutex with that name (CreateMutexW fails with ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE), and a stock launch will simply replace the tray process.
The local HKCU Run key has no Roblox entry right now; where auto-start is written is unknown. That the tray process's command line literally contains --launch-to-tray is inferred from the binary string.

findings.claim: All clients share %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\LocalStorage\RobloxCookies.dat and appStorage.json. The client reads and writes them at startup, so the last-launched account's state leaks into other clients and into the user's normal Roblox app session.
findings.detail:
Local observations:
- RobloxCookies.dat (2,351 bytes) is JSON with top-level keys CookiesVersion and CookiesData; the data is encrypted, and values were not read.
- appStorage.json top-level keys include AccountBlob, WebLogin, BrowserTrackerId, PlayerExeLaunchTime, SystemTrayModalShown, NativeCloseLuaPromptDisplayCount (per-user map {default, u_<userId>}) and UpdateControllerCache*.
- Both files' modification times match the last client launch (2026-10-24 01:00 local).
- Startup log lines: "[FLog::LogWin32BTId] LogWin32BTId, App, cookie Native => Engine set RBXEventTrackerV2 as CreateDate=...&rbxid=<userId>&rbxuid=<id>&browserid=<btid>" and later "cookie Engine => Native set RBXEventTrackerV2 ...". So the tracker cookie with the previous user's id is loaded from the shared store and written back.
Community evidence:
- evanovar #83 (2026-10-12, client 0.742): during a bulk launch with no file protection, Account A's client read native tracking state with Account B's id, received HTTP 403 "challengedByGcs" from game-join, and showed Account B's name above the CAPTCHA. Account A was then locked; the reporter says causation is not established.
- evanovar #85: the wrong displayed identity followed access to the shared appStorage.json and went away while that file was held exclusively.
- Teleport error 773 / "512 (Unauthorized)" for every client except the most recently launched one: DevForum 2324412 (May 2023, client 0.574) and MultiBloxy #3 (Dec 2024). The fix is to lock RobloxCookies.dat: niccsprojects/Roblox-Account-Manager PR #47 (2026-04-09), MultiAlt ('fix 773'), and evanovar (CreateFile(GENERIC_READ, share 0, OPEN_ALWAYS) plus a byte-range lock over 0x7fffffff bytes on both files while multi mode is on, taken only while Roblox is closed).
- Bloxstrap #5841 (2025-09): the first client stops loading new assets once a second starts. This fits the same cause but is inferred.
Whether launching B invalidates A's server-side session: no evidence that it does. The damage is local shared state.
sources: local: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\LocalStorage (key names only) and Player logs

findings.claim: Roblox has made no official statement that allows or bans multiple clients. The only Roblox-sounding statement (May 2023) calls it unsupported and liable to be blocked. Third parties report active countermeasures since mid-2025.
findings.detail:
- DevForum topic 2324412: user ScipioAfrikanos, 2023-05-11, wrote "Unfortunately like you said this isn't supported behavior" and advised against building workflows on it, as it "may change or be blocked at anytime". The post speaks as 'we', but the forum JSON today shows staff=false and no title (that flag covers only forum admins and moderators), so Roblox employment is unconfirmed. The thread metadata is saved as a fixture.
- DevForum topics 3069535 (Jul 2024) and 3730867 (Jun 2025, replies to Aug 2026) have no staff answer.
- Bloxstrap v2.10.0 notes (2025-10-01): Roblox has "been cracking down on multi-instance launching and now have preventative anti-measures for it".
- The MultiBloxy README (since 2025-08-01) says: "Roblox is actively blocking multi-instance tools".
- Reports of clients closing after about 30 minutes: MultiBloxy #6 (2025-06-11), Bloxstrap #5579 (2025-07-28) and #5890 (2025-10-01, 'if you autoclicked it would run'). The cause is unconfirmed; the standard 20-minute idle kick on unfocused windows is a plausible alternative.
- Roblox ships alt-account detection in the Ban API (DevForum announcement 3039740, mid-2024), and creators can extend bans to suspected alts. Users report terminations for shared device or IP (DevForum 4230125, community).

findings.claim: Process model: with the stock install the roblox-player: (and roblox:) handler is RobloxPlayerBeta.exe itself, and there is no separate launcher. Spawning that exe with CreateProcess and the URI as the argument gives RoALT the client PID. Bootstrappers (Bloxstrap and forks) register themselves instead and spawn their own copy of the client.
findings.detail:
Registry, read locally:
- HKCU\Software\Classes\roblox-player\shell\open\command (Default) = "%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Roblox\Versions\version-9ac8595712b447a7\RobloxPlayerBeta.exe" %1, with value version=version-9ac8595712b447a7. The roblox protocol key is identical.
- HKCU\Software\ROBLOX Corporation\Environments\roblox-player has (Default)=...\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe, clientExe=...\RobloxPlayerBeta.exe, version and baseHost=www.roblox.com. clientExe is the cleanest source for the official client path.
Bloxstrap registers "<Bloxstrap.exe>" -player "%1" (WindowsRegistry.RegisterPlayer) and starts its own Versions copy of RobloxPlayerBeta.exe with Arguments=<the URI> (Fishstrap Bootstrapper.cs StartRoblox). If RoALT launches through such a handler, the PID it gets is the bootstrapper's, not the client's.
MultiAlt, Fishstrap and Bloxstrap all start RobloxPlayerBeta.exe directly with the URI as the only argument. The client itself starts its updater as "<versionDir>\RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe" roblox-player:1+launchmode:play+gameinfo:<ticket>+launchtime:<ms>+LaunchExp:InApp+gameLocale:en_us+robloxLocale:en_us+browsertrackerid:<id>+placelauncherurl:<urlencoded> (local log line "[FLog::UpdateController] Update thread: start ...").
The legacy argument form still exists in the binary (" --app", " -t {}"); MultiAlt's 'old join' uses RobloxPlayerBeta.exe --app -t <ticket> -j <PlaceLauncher url>.
Child and companion processes per client:
- RobloxCrashHandler.exe (crashpad; its own *_Player_<hex>_CrashHandler_last.log, with flags --database=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs\crashes --url=https://upload.crashes.rbxinfra.com/post...);
- RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe when an update is needed;
- a --launch-to-tray RobloxPlayerBeta.exe on close (see M5);
- WebView2 children for challenge and CAPTCHA pages (evanovar #83).

findings.claim: An outdated version folder normally does not change the PID: the client checks clientsettingscdn, picks BACKGROUND update mode, keeps running into the game, and starts RobloxPlayerInstaller.exe in the background. A FOREGROUND update (for example a channel mismatch) closes every running RobloxPlayerBeta.exe and relaunches, so PIDs change and other accounts die.
findings.detail:
- Local log 20261023T220008Z (0.743 binary, server version 0.744): "version response: {\"version\":\"0.744.0.7441080\",\"clientVersionUpload\":\"version-9ac8595712b447a7\",\"bootstrapperVersion\":\"\"}", then "updateRequired TRUE", then "Update mode is chosen as BACKGROUND". The client still joined the game at +1.66 s.
- The installer log RobloxPlayerInstaller_ADA07.log ("The installer will run InstallUpdate", BITS jobs, "Set the launcher for Roblox as ...") finished at +10.7 s and rewrote the handler to version-9ac8595712b447a7. No second Player log appeared, so there was no relaunch.
- Captured endpoint: GET https://clientsettingscdn.roblox.com/v2/client-version/WindowsPlayer returns 200 with that same JSON; headers include Cache-Control: public, must-revalidate, max-age=30, X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000, 5000;w=1 and Rbx-Cdn-Provider: ak. The .../channel/LIVE variant returns the same.
- MultiAlt launch.rs (2026-09/10): accounts enrolled in a non-production channel cause a background install that rewrites the handler and registry channel. The next launch with a mismatched build reports updateRequired TRUE and runs a FOREGROUND installer that "closes every running RobloxPlayerBeta.exe". The URI's channel: field overrides the registry ("channel:" empty means production).
- evanovar #92 (2026-10-19): during startup a client process can exit and a replacement with the same launch tracker appear moments later. They allow re-binding within 120 s.
- Bloxstrap 'Background updates' (2025-03-13) also exists.
- Old version folders stay on disk: 4 present locally.

findings.claim: Mapping a client and its log file to an account: launch with a unique browsertrackerid per launch. The client logs it as websiteBTId, it appears in the process command line, and the game_join_loadtime line carries userid, which confirms the authenticated account.
findings.detail:
Confirmed local line formats:
- "[FLog::LogWin32BTId] LogWin32BTId, App, web launch, websiteBTId is <btid>"
- "[FLog::AppRemoteCheckStarterModule] BTID is overriden to <btid>."
- "[FLog::GameJoinLoadTime] Report game_join_loadtime: placeid:<n>, join_time:<f>, universeid:<n>, referral_page:<RequestGame|RequestPrivateGame|RequestFollowUser|...>, sid:<uuid>, clienttime:<f>, userid:<n>, ..."
- "[FLog::Output] ! Joining game '<jobId uuid>' place <placeId> at <ip>"
evanovar launch_monitor.py matches the process via psutil cmdline() with regex browsertrackerid[^0-9]{0,32}(\d+), the log via 'web launch, websiteBTId is (\d+)', and the account via \[FLog::GameJoinLoadTime\].*\buserid:(\d+). It reports ROBLOX_ACCOUNT_MISMATCH when userid differs and ROBLOX_SECURITY_CHALLENGE when the log contains 'challengedByGcs'.
PID to log file: the log name is <version>_<yyyymmddThhmmssZ>_Player_<5 hex>_last.log, and the hex does not look like the PID (unverified). Approaches in use: Bloxstrap takes the newest 'Player' log created within 15 s; Fishstrap uses a FileSystemWatcher for the first *.log created after Process.Start (but a _CrashHandler_last.log is created in the same second, so exclude it); Roblox Account Manager and evanovar read the process's open file handles (handle.exe or psutil open_files, which duplicates Roblox handles, so it is out of scope for RoALT).
The command line includes gameinfo:<auth ticket>. WMI Win32_Process.CommandLine therefore exposes the ticket to any same-user process (tickets are short-lived) and must never be logged.

findings.claim: Bloxstrap's activity-watcher markers, checked against the current source and local logs. Most log files end with no exit marker when the user closes the window, so a process-exit signal is needed alongside the log.
findings.detail:
Bloxstrap ActivityWatcher.cs (last changed 2026-08-05) uses: GameJoiningEntry "[FLog::Output] ! Joining game" with pattern ! Joining game '([0-9a-f\-]{36})' place ([0-9]+) at ([0-9\.]+); GameJoiningUniverseEntry "[FLog::GameJoinLoadTime] Report game_join_loadtime:" with universeid:([0-9]+).*userid:([0-9]+); GameJoiningUDMUXEntry "[FLog::Network] UDMUX Address = "; GameJoinedEntry "[FLog::Network] Replicator created: " (changed from 'serverId:' on 2026-04-04 for RbxTransport); GameDisconnectedEntry "[FLog::Network] Time to disconnect replication data:"; GameLeavingEntry "[FLog::SingleSurfaceApp] leaveUGCGameInternal"; GameTeleportingEntry "[FLog::UgcExperienceController] UgcExperienceController: doTeleport: joinScriptUrl"; GameMessageEntry "[FLog::CreatorOutput] [BloxstrapRPC]". It polls the file at 1 s, opened with FileShare.ReadWrite.
Other lines seen locally: "[FLog::Network] Disconnection Notification. Reason: 267", "[FLog::Network] Lost connection with reason : You have been kicked from the game", "[FLog::Network] Sending disconnect with reason: 267", "[DFLog::RbxTransportDummyClient] Disconnected from server for reason: Player: 285 (DisconnectClientInitiated)", "... Connection closed by server for reason: RCC: 288 (DisconnectServerShutdown)", and "[DFLog::NetworkClient] Client:Disconnect".
The local line prefix is <ISO UTC>,<secs since start>,<thread hex>,<level digit>[,<Info|Warning|Error|Critical|Debug>] <message>.
In 40 recent Player logs, user-closed sessions end with routine lines (FlagCache, D3D11) and no shutdown marker. 'shutDown:' and 'leaveUGCGameInternal' appear only for replacement or tray exits. After a kick or disconnect the process keeps running with the error dialog.

findings.claim: Holding a full-access process handle to RobloxPlayerBeta.exe for long has tripped Hyperion before. Maintained tools close the CreateProcess handle immediately and detect exit by polling the process list, which means no exit code is available.
findings.detail:
- Bloxstrap commit 6ea198f1 (2023-04-20, 'Fix Byfron crashes'): "byfron will trip if you keep a process handle for robloxplayerbeta open for any longer than a minute". It disposes the Process right after reading Id and loops on Process.GetProcesses().Any(x => x.Id == pid) every 1 s. The comment survives in Fishstrap Bootstrapper.cs ("v2.2.0 - byfron will trip if we keep a process handle open for over a minute"). Since then Bloxstrap no longer logs an ExitCode.
- MultiAlt polls with CreateToolhelp32Snapshot and opens short-lived handles: PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION for memory, PROCESS_TERMINATE then TerminateProcess(h, 1) then CloseHandle.
- evanovar checks identity as (pid, create_time) to survive PID reuse.
Whether a long-held SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION handle is tolerated today is unverified. Exit codes for normal close, crash or kick are unknown: no source documents them, and no RobloxPlayerBeta Application Error (1000/1001) events exist locally. Crash signal: crashpad database at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs\crashes (reports\, attachments\, settings.dat). New report files there would indicate a crash; that is inferred.

findings.claim: Closing instances: tools use WM_CLOSE (CloseMainWindow) for a graceful close and TerminateProcess to force. A graceful close lets the server see the disconnect; killing can leave the server-side session alive, so relaunching the same account soon after may hit 'Same account launched'.
findings.detail:
- Bloxstrap Watcher.CloseProcess(pid, force): force calls process.Kill(), otherwise process.CloseMainWindow(). It also calls CloseMainWindow on the OnAppClose event (leaveUGCGameInternal).
- Roblox Account Manager (AutoCloseLastProcess) sends CloseMainWindow, waits 250 ms, sends it again, waits 250 ms, then Kill(), commented "Allows Roblox to disconnect from the server so we don't get the 'Same account launched' error". That this is Roblox error 273 is from memory and not verified here.
- Fishstrap KillRobloxPlayers kills both RobloxPlayerBeta and RobloxCrashHandler before updating.
- MultiAlt kill_for_user calls TerminateProcess and waits up to 1.2 s.
Caveats: appStorage.json key NativeCloseLuaPromptDisplayCount suggests a native 'leave?' prompt can appear on close (inferred), which would explain the double WM_CLOSE. In tray-treatment builds a WM_CLOSE may spawn a --launch-to-tray process (M5).

open_questions: Exact current single-instance algorithm: the order of CreateEvent/SetEvent/CreateMutex/WaitForSingleObject and its timeouts. Also what the newer SingleInstanceGuard '{}.mtx'/'{}.shm' names resolve to, and whether it forwards deep links to an existing window instead of starting a new client. Only strings and log lines were seen; nothing was disassembled.

Does the client log 'Cannot create event to secure single process' and keep running normally when RoALT pre-holds a mutex named ROBLOX_singletonEvent? Inferred from tools that work in Oct 2026; not seen in a local log.

Is pre-holding ROBLOX_singletonMutex still useful alongside the ROBLOX_singletonEvent mutex, or harmful (could a new client block in waitForNewPlayerProcess until a timeout)? evanovar holds both and MultiAlt reports clients start while another program holds the mutex, but the timeout value is unknown.

Exit codes of RobloxPlayerBeta.exe for normal close, crash and kick are undocumented. Also unknown: whether Hyperion tolerates a long-held SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION handle; the only evidence is from 2023 and concerns full-access handles.

What is inside RobloxCookies.dat (encrypted CookiesData) after a ticket launch: does it persist the launched account's .ROBLOSECURITY? If so, the user's normal Roblox app session is replaced by the last launched alt. Strongly suggested by Froststrap/Onyxstrap behaviour; not decrypted or verified.
Where the tray treatment writes its auto-start entry (the local HKCU Run key has none), and whether a --launch-to-tray process can be running at Windows logon before RoALT starts.
Whether the 30-40 minute closures of extra clients (2025 reports) are a Roblox countermeasure or the normal 20-minute idle kick for unfocused windows.
Whether ScipioAfrikanos (May 2023 'not supported' reply) was Roblox staff; the forum profile shows no title today.
design_implications: Singleton guard: before the first client starts, call CreateMutexW(NULL, TRUE, L"ROBLOX_singletonEvent") with the exact case and no Global\ prefix (Local\ is equivalent). Optionally also CreateMutexW(NULL, TRUE, L"ROBLOX_singletonMutex"). Own both on one long-lived dedicated thread so ReleaseMutex works and the mutex is never abandoned. If CreateMutexW returns ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE or ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS, a Roblox process (possibly a tray process) already owns the name. Refuse multi-launch and offer to close the existing RobloxPlayerBeta.exe instead of touching its handles.
Before enabling multi-launch, list RobloxPlayerBeta.exe processes (Toolhelp32 snapshot) and treat any whose command line contains --launch-to-tray as Roblox's tray process, not an account client.

Launch by CreateProcessW on the official client path: read HKCU\Software\ROBLOX Corporation\Environments\roblox-player\clientExe, falling back to the roblox-player handler only if it points at RobloxPlayerBeta.exe. Pass the full roblox-player: URI as the single argument and keep 'channel:' empty for production. If the handler is Bloxstrap/Fishstrap/Voidstrap, either refuse or note that the PID belongs to the bootstrapper.

Close hProcess/hThread from CreateProcess immediately and track clients by (PID, creation time) polling every ~1 s, as Bloxstrap has done since 2023. Treat exit codes as unavailable. If a waitable handle is ever used, request only SYNCHRONIZE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, behind a setting.

Generate a unique browsertrackerid per launch. Bind the log file by finding the '_Player_' log (not '_CrashHandler_') created after spawn that contains 'web launch, websiteBTId is <btid>'. Confirm the account with 'userid:<id>' in the game_join_loadtime line, and pause bulk launch on 'challengedByGcs' or a userid mismatch.

Serialize bulk launches: wait for the previous client's log binding, plus ideally its join or main window, before the next CreateProcess. Allow a replacement process with the same tracker to re-bind within about 120 s (update handoff), with no automatic relaunch.
Never log the process command line: it contains gameinfo:<auth ticket>.

Offer optional 'shared login protection': while multi-launch is active and only while Roblox is closed, open RobloxCookies.dat and appStorage.json with share mode 0 and hold them. Warn that Roblox and bootstrapper account switchers then cannot persist logins, and release when the last tracked client exits.

Session state from logs: 'Joining game' then 'Replicator created' means in game. 'Time to disconnect replication data', 'Disconnection Notification', 'Lost connection with reason' or 'Disconnected from server for reason' mean disconnected, but the process may stay open. Process gone means exited, since user closes usually leave no log marker. 'EventWaitResultUpdate' plus 'Received close main window request' means another launch replaced this client.

Close instance: post WM_CLOSE to the client's main window (repeat once after ~250-500 ms in case a leave prompt appears), wait a few seconds, then TerminateProcess(PROCESS_TERMINATE, short-lived handle). Expect a --launch-to-tray process to possibly appear afterwards.

Show users a risk notice: multi-client is unsupported by Roblox ('may be blocked at any time', 2023), tools report active countermeasures since mid-2025, and account locks were seen during bulk launches with shared state (Oct 2026), causation unproven.
